give_baseline.modeled_endpoint: temperature-associated net all-cause mortality monetized with VSL

primary_method_source.citation: Cromar et al. (2022), Global Health Impacts for Economic Models of Climate Change: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
findings: The pooled outcome is temperature-associated net all-cause mortality risk.
The review reports that air pollution was often treated as a potential mediator in studies assessing temperature-health risk.
The expert panel identifies a separate air-pollution module as useful while emphasizing interaction and baseline-emissions complexity.

overlap_assessment.wildfire_smoke_vs_wildfire_co2_reason: Direct smoke mortality and downstream warming damages from wildfire CO2 are different endpoints, but the smoke estimate remains operationally unreproduced.
overlap_assessment.mcduffie_boundary_reason: McDuffie explicitly excludes open-burning emissions including wildfires.
overlap_assessment.uncleared_reason: GIVE's source outcome is net all-cause mortality and its evidence base may include air pollution as mediator or effect modifier; no source-study decomposition or replacement adjustment is available.

decision.required_resolution: Estimate or obtain a mutually exclusive temperature-mortality baseline, or implement and validate a replacement joint mortality module that allocates temperature and air-pollution pathways once.
